extracted.intended_audience: authors and researchers considering publishing books or journals with Springer
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level criteria for authors choosing to publish books, book series, journal articles, or respond to calls for papers with Springer, including metrics, series/collection fit, and available author resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing model
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing model — e.g., Hybrid, Open access (as shown on journal entries: 'Publishing model Hybrid' / 'Publishing model Open access').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates whether a journal is hybrid or open access; relevant for authors deciding on access, charges, and dissemination options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Impact Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Impact Factor — numeric value with year (example: 'Journal Impact Factor 2.8 (2024)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a measure of journal influence or prestige; authors may use it to assess fit and perceived impact of publishing in the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downloads
rubrics_metrics.description: Downloads — total or annual download counts (examples: 'Downloads 1.6M (2025)', 'Downloads 242.4k (2025)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to indicate reach and readership; informs authors about potential visibility and readership levels for published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to first decision (median)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission to first decision (median) — time from submission to initial editorial decision (example: 'Submission to first decision (median) 32 days').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A speed/turnaround metric that helps authors evaluate how quickly a journal handles submissions; may influence where to submit based on desired timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls for papers — Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for papers status — indicates whether a collection or call is open, invitation-only, or otherwise (examples: 'Status Open for submissions', 'RILEM TC 314-OCM: ON-SITE... (Invitation only)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals eligibility to submit; some calls are open while others are invitation-only, affecting whether authors can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calls for papers — Submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission deadline — explicit date by which submissions must be received for a collection or call (examples: 'Submission deadline 28 December 2030', 'Submission deadline 15 December 2029').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural requirement that determines timeliness and eligibility; authors must meet deadlines to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection/topic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection scope and thematic alignment — descriptions of what a Collection seeks (examples: 'This Collection presents the Recommendations prepared by the RILEM Technical Committee 314-OCM (On-site corrosion condition assessment...)', 'We are calling for articles to our new Collection on Partnership for the Goals, in support of the UN Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must align with the stated thematic scope of a Collection or special issue; relevance to the theme is a core acceptance criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book series scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Book series scope — short statements about what a series includes (example: 'This series includes collective thematic books and monographs on advanced research topics in continuum mechanics').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should match the subject matter and type of work (e.g., monograph, thematic collective) to the stated scope when proposing a book for a series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for book authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for book authors — availability of guidance and tools (text: 'Find guidance and tools to help you develop, enhance, and promote your book').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer provides author resources for manuscript development, enhancement, and promotion; authors are encouraged to use these tools to improve quality and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher value proposition (reach, credibility, support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher positioning — Springer 'empowers authors to share impactful research, enable readers to access trusted content, and collaborate with institutions... provides the reach, credibility, and support to help your work make a lasting difference.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are being asked to consider publisher-level benefits (reach, credibility, institutional partnerships, support services) when choosing where to publish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured content as exemplars of suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured books and journals presented as exemplars (e.g., lists of 'Featured books', 'Featured book series', and 'Featured journals' with descriptions of their focus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples illustrate the kinds of books, series, and journals Springer considers appropriate for its portfolio — useful for authors to gauge fit and expected quality/subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject coverage / journal categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals by subject — categorical listing of subject areas (examples: 'Behavioral Sciences and Psychology', 'Biological Sciences', 'Chemistry', 'Computer Science', etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should identify the appropriate subject category to find journals or book series that match their work; subject fit is a primary selection criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission model and submission routes
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission options referenced (e.g., 'Submit your book idea', 'Submit an article', 'Publish a book', 'Publishing options').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates multiple routes and formats for publishing (book proposals, article submission, language-specific publishing); authors must follow the appropriate submission path and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-facing guidance on promotion and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Author guidance content examples (blog titles: 'How to master SEO for books: A guide for authors', 'Promote your book: Social media strategies for authors', 'How to promote your book through networking and sharing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer provides editorial/marketing advice to help authors increase discoverability; authors are encouraged to follow best practices in SEO, social media, and networking to promote their work.
